title: Motorola's new Signature 27 has it all if you can stomach the $1,600 price tag
gist: Motorola announced the Signature 27, a non-folding US flagship with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a 12,000-nit tandem OLED and a 7,000 mAh battery, priced at $1,600, above Samsung and Apple flagships and within $300 of $1,900 foldables. It is a full Gemini Intelligence device and the first Moto phone supporting user-installed GrapheneOS, on sale November 26 without carrier partners.

insights.claim: Motorola's Signature 27 costs $1,600, above high-end flagships from Samsung and Apple and within $300 of the $1,900 Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Motorola Razr Fold, which the author attributes partly to high-end hardware costs in the age of AI.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Signals rising smartphone ASPs and component cost pressure, while risking cannibalization of Motorola's own foldable.
